title: Model-Lab Next Blocker Triage v1
description: Machine-readable artifact that prioritizes the remaining result-assessment blockers of a Model-Lab series and recommends which blocker to address next. It is a methodological prioritization only: it deliberately does NOT resolve any blocker, does NOT remediate dependency risk, does NOT start a new run, does NOT allow a result_assessment, and does NOT make the series comparison-ready. It records triage_status, that result_assessment/comparison stay blocked after triage, the source evidence it is anchored to, the prioritized remaining blockers, a recommended next task, and an anti-overclaim does_not_establish boundary. Form is validated here; semantic rules (referenced readiness gate must confirm a blocked assessment, result_assessment/comparison must stay false, recommended next task present, the remaining_blockers id set must match the dependency-risk-scope remaining_blockers, source-evidence existence/escape, mandatory does_not_establish) are enforced by scripts/docmeta/validate_model_lab_next_blocker_triage.py.

triage_status.$comment: v1 models exactly one real status: complete. A triage artifact is only emitted once the prioritization is done. Semantic rules keep result_assessment_allowed_after_triage=false and comparison_ready_after_triage=false; triage prioritizes, it does not unblock.

result_assessment_allowed_after_triage.$comment: In v1 this must be false. true is rejected by the validator (TRIAGE_REQUIRES_FALSE_RESULT_ASSESSMENT_ALLOWED); a triage prioritizes blockers, it does not authorize a result assessment.

comparison_ready_after_triage.$comment: In v1 this must be false. true is rejected by the validator (TRIAGE_REQUIRES_FALSE_COMPARISON_READY); a triage does not make the series comparison-ready.

source_evidence.$comment: At least one entry must be a readiness_gate that the validator can read and that confirms result_assessment is still blocked (TRIAGE_REQUIRES_BLOCKED_ASSESSMENT).

remaining_blockers.$comment: Each entry must stay status=open (TRIAGE_REQUIRES_OPEN_REMAINING_BLOCKERS). The id set must exactly match the dependency-risk-caveat-scope artifact's remaining_blockers (TRIAGE_REQUIRES_ALL_SCOPE_BLOCKERS); the expected ids are read from that artifact, not hardcoded here.

recommended_next_task.$comment: Schema-optional so that an omitted task is reported as a stable semantic rule (TRIAGE_REQUIRES_RECOMMENDED_NEXT_TASK) rather than a raw schema error. When present, id, target_blocker, and reason must be non-empty (validator).

does_not_establish.$comment: Mandatory anti-overclaim list. Must include the baseline non-claims enforced by the validator: result_assessment_allowed, comparison_ready, security_readiness, production_readiness, model_quality, comparative_superiority, condition_effect, external_model_independence, external_auditor_comparison_completed, dependency_risk_remediated.

repoRelativePath.$comment: Repo-relative POSIX path. Absolute paths, drive letters and backslashes are rejected here; parent-escape ('..') and symlink-out-of-repo are rejected semantically by the validator with a stable rule id.

kind.$comment: Provenance label, e.g. readiness_gate, dependency_risk_scope, assessment_context, result_summary. The validator cross-checks 'readiness_gate' (must be a blocked result_assessment_readiness artifact for this series) and 'dependency_risk_scope' (must be a dependency_risk_caveat_scope artifact for this series, source of the expected blocker set).

status.$comment: 'resolved' is form-valid but semantically rejected by the validator (TRIAGE_REQUIRES_OPEN_REMAINING_BLOCKERS) so the rejection emits a stable rule id rather than a raw schema error.
